authority.owner_requirements: This file records explicit 5fedu product behavior supplied by the owner.
authority.source_observation: Exact component structure, styling, routes, fields, permissions and runtime behavior remain source-derived.
authority.rule: Owner requirements constrain adaptation; they never replace a verified source receipt or active project schema/spec.
authority.reference_policy: Read source by pointer from the harness. Do not copy the reference template into target projects and do not treat reference code as target business requirements.
authority.anti_anchor: Reference implementation supplies patterns/evidence, not mandatory feature inventory; active project requirements and schema decide what applies.

owner_requirements.statement: Use the Employee module as the canonical internal-entity list/detail/form/statistics shell.
List view provides the source-supported Back, filter/search controls, Add, Import and Export actions; do not invent duplicate actions.
The list has the canonical pagination footer when the source surface is paginated.
Status and other categorical list values use the canonical bounded/badge treatment when the source does.
The action column keeps the source-aligned visible Edit action plus overflow menu; Delete lives in overflow and requires confirmation.
Detail drawer follows the canonical hero + information sections + related/tab surfaces.
Detail toolbar contains only meaningful business workflow actions such as approve/status changes when supported; do not duplicate ordinary Edit/Delete controls already owned elsewhere.
Create/Edit form mirrors the detail drawer information architecture, adapted only for editable controls and validation.
Statistics reuse the canonical Employee statistics pattern and are adapted to the target module rather than replaced by an invented dashboard.
Department is the organizational parent axis; default depth is two levels unless the active project spec explicitly differs.
Department detail drawer contains subordinate department and related-data tables when those relations exist in the active schema/source.
Nested child rows follow the canonical action-column pattern including source-aligned Edit plus overflow/Delete confirmation.
Nested tables expose a toolbar only for real business actions; do not duplicate generic Edit/Delete controls.
Classify subordinate hierarchy separately from related modules/tabs using source/schema relations; never infer relation semantics from visual similarity.
Permission coverage must be derived from and reconcile with the active module/route registry; every permission-bearing module must be represented.
Permission actions and scopes come from active project contracts; do not infer approval from edit or fabricate missing rights.

relationship_rules.statement: Position is related to the Department organizational axis; exact cardinality and UI placement come from the active source/schema.
Subordinate hierarchy and related data are different semantic relations and must be represented separately when both exist.
